subject: Lumenpay SSO cutover — timeline
snippet: Dev — we're finalizing our Q4 enterprise launch plan on our side and the board is asking hard questions about our own vendor dependencies, Kettle included. Our security team flagge
body_text:
Dev — we're finalizing our Q4 enterprise launch plan on our side and the board is asking hard questions about our own vendor dependencies, Kettle included. Our security team flagged that our current SAML setup with Kettle is a stopgap, and we need proper SSO/SAML enforcement before we can onboard the next 200 seats — our compliance team won't sign off on expanding seat count without it.

Can you give me a real, committed date for when Kettle can ship SSO enforcement for enterprise workspaces? I know we've talked about this informally a few times since the spring — first at the QBR in April, then again when Dev mentioned it offhand on the SLA call in May — but nothing ever turned into an actual date on a calendar. I need something I can put in front of our board on the 15th of next month. If it slips again it puts our whole rollout timeline at risk, and honestly it starts to look bad for both of us given how much we've publicly talked about the Kettle partnership internally, including in our own investor updates.

For context on why this matters more than it might have a quarter ago: we signed two new enterprise logos last month who both have security questionnaires that explicitly require SSO/SAML enforcement on every vendor that touches customer data, and Kettle is on that list for both of them. Our own compliance team has started asking pointed questions about why we're still running mixed auth with a vendor at our scale. I've been running interference on this for a while, but I'm genuinely running out of runway to keep saying 'soon.'

There's also a practical piece: our provisioning workflow for new seats currently requires someone on my team to manually add each user because we can't rely on directory sync without proper SAML, which doesn't scale past a few hundred seats without someone burning a day a week on user admin. That alone is reason enough for us to want this fixed independent of the compliance angle.

Also — separately, our finance team asked if there's flexibility on the per-seat pricing once we cross 400 seats, given the direction things are trending on our side. Not urgent, just flagging it exists so it's not a surprise later.

Appreciate you, know everyone's slammed on both sides right now. Let's just get a real date on the books so I stop having to give my board a vague answer every time this comes up.

Dana

subject: Foundry Line — next steps
snippet: Maya — great catching up last week. Wanted to follow up in writing on where Foundry Line stands. We're genuinely excited about Kettle and think there's a strong case internally to
body_text:
Maya — great catching up last week. Wanted to follow up in writing on where Foundry Line stands. We're genuinely excited about Kettle and think there's a strong case internally to lead a Series B, but our investment committee is going to want to see a couple of things before we get too far down the path: a clean view of gross retention across your top 10 accounts, and some comfort on the customer concentration question given how much of your ARR sits with Lumenpay right now. Neither of those is a dealbreaker, just table stakes for us to build a real case internally.

To give you a sense of process on our end: once we have the retention data and the technical diligence call, we'd take it to a partner meeting, most likely the one in three weeks given our calendar. If that goes well, we'd move to a term sheet conversation fairly quickly — we don't like to drag diligence out once we've decided we're serious, and internally people are already saying good things after the first two conversations. I'd rather be transparent about the shape of the process now than have you guessing at where things stand later.

On the retention data specifically — doesn't need to be a polished deck, a raw export from your billing system with logo-level ARR by month for the last six quarters would be plenty for our associate to build the cohort view we need. If it's easier, Wendy could send it directly to our analyst rather than routing through you. Our associate's name is Priya Chandrasekaran — I'll have her reach out directly so this doesn't have to go through me for something this administrative.

One more thing — could you loop in Dev for a quick technical diligence call before Friday? Our partner doing the tech review has a narrow window and Friday is really the only slot that works before he's out for two weeks. He'll mostly want to understand the architecture around multi-tenancy and how you're handling the SOC2 work, since that tends to be the thing later-stage enterprise customers care most about.

Otherwise, no rush on anything else — happy to keep the conversation going at whatever pace makes sense for you given everything else on your plate right now. I know fundraising while running the company is its own particular flavor of exhausting, and I'd rather this feel collaborative than like one more deadline stacked on top of everything else you're juggling this quarter.

snippet: Team, Wanted to get everyone aligned before things get busier with the board meeting and the audit converging in the next two weeks. Runway: we're sitting around 11.5 months at cur
body_text:
Team,

Wanted to get everyone aligned before things get busier with the board meeting and the audit converging in the next two weeks.

Runway: we're sitting around 11.5 months at current burn, which is fine but not generous — the Lumenpay renewal and the seat expansion Tom's been working matter more to that number than anything else on the table right now. If the 450-seat figure holds, that materially extends our runway and makes the Series B conversation a want-to, not a need-to. If it slips back down, we should assume we're raising by Q1 regardless of how the Foundry Line conversation goes.

Lumenpay: I made a commitment to Dana on the SSO date that I'm now walking back because of the SOC2 timeline collision. I take responsibility for that — we shouldn't have promised a firm date before checking it against the audit schedule, and I want us to be more disciplined about that going forward, especially with Dana given how much weight our relationship carries with their own board.

SOC2: evidence deadline moved up to the 13th per Rachel's note. Wendy and Priya, I know this is going to be a rough week, thank you in advance. If there's anything I can personally take off either of your plates to make that number, say so directly and I'll rearrange.

Hiring: the Head of Marketing search is moving — Alice sent over four strong candidates and we've got first rounds Friday. I'd like Sana and Luis in the room for at least one of those given how much of this role touches brand and product marketing together.

Board meeting: Aug 27, usual format. Sana's pulling the deck together — please get her what she's asked for on time this cycle, we were scrambling at the printer last quarter and I'd like to not repeat that.

Foundry Line: early-stage Series B conversation, nothing to announce, but Raj's team is doing real diligence, not just a warm intro call. Dev, you may hear from me about a technical diligence session with their partner soon — they'll mostly want to talk multi-tenancy architecture and SOC2 status, so it's worth having Priya on that call too.

AWS: the bill spike from June is fully explained now — it was the autoscaling group misconfiguration Priya patched last week, not organic usage growth, so there's no change to our unit economics story for the board deck. Wendy already has the credit that came back from AWS reflected in the runway model Peter sent over.

One more thing on Lumenpay specifically: the seat count on their renewal has moved around more than I'd like over the last month — 400, then 320, now apparently 450 with an EU buffer — and I don't want us building the board deck around whichever number happened to be the most recent one Tom heard on a call. Tom, can you get something in writing from Dana before it goes in the deck.

That's it for now. Appreciate everyone's work through what's been a genuinely hard stretch of overlapping deadlines — let's get through the next three weeks and then I owe the team a real breather.

Maya
